fatal_errors: The cited studies provide room-temperature mechanical properties but do not support the claimed approximately 20% yield-strength improvement at 800–900 °C.
The proposed Ti-rich medium-entropy alloy and single-phase Zr intervention do not reconstruct the target Cr-modified HfMoTaTiZr refractory alloy or its reticulated Laves-phase mechanism.
The hypothesis treats secondary-phase formation as falsifying, whereas the target improvement depends on approximately 4 vol.% of a specifically reticulated Laves phase.
explanation: This is a testable lightweight-alloy alternative, but it differs fundamentally from the hidden target. The target adds 4.2 at.% Cr to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, producing an interconnected Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves phase and lattice contraction; the generated hypothesis instead adds about 7 at.% Zr to Ti65(AlCrNbV), aiming to retain a single BCC phase. There is limited mechanistic overlap through substitutional solid-solution hardening and lattice distortion, but the crucial crack-arrest and plasticity-compensation role of the reticulated Laves phase is absent. The paired-alloy experiment, phase characterization, density measurement, and explicit falsification threshold are reasonably discriminating. However, evidence E1–E4 supports low density, single-phase BCC structure, Zr-induced atomic-size mismatch, and strong room-temperature tensile behavior—not elevated-temperature strength retention or a 20% improvement over a Zr-free baseline at 800 °C. Thus the central jet-turbine-temperature outcome is speculative rather than evidence-backed.
